title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operating in autonomous mode struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while a human safety operator was present in the vehicle. The vehicle did not slow down or stop. This shows a failure in the system's object recognition or decision-making: the car did not identify the duck as an obstacle requiring avoidance or did not generate a command to brake. What would have caught this is either pre-deployment testing that included small animals in its obstacle detection validation, or a safety operator who could intervene when the system failed to recognize a hazard.

A resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though the company disputed this after reviewing data. It is not established whether this second claim is accurate. The incident prompted the operator to exclude certain routes from testing and to run simulations evaluating changes to the technology, but it is not established what specific technical improvements, if any, were implemented or whether they addressed the duck strike itself.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant concern from residents. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without stopping or slowing down. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant, making it familiar to neighbors. A resident posted about the incident on a neighborhood Facebook group, also claiming the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data.

Following the backlash, Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its autonomous vehicle routes. The company is now evaluating potential improvements to its technology to avoid similar incidents in the future, running controlled simulations to ensure any changes do not compromise safety performance. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, are also actively testing or deploying vehicles in Austin.
